Report the design and fitted sample for NIS analyses

Source: R/design-report.R
nis_design_report.Rd

Reads the sampling metadata retained by nis_design() without querying the original data. Use it on the design after a domain filter, or on a survey::svyglm() fit from that design to see the fitted sample size.

Usage

nis_design_report(x)

Arguments

x

A nis_design() result, including a filtered or reweighted design, or a survey::svyglm() fit made with that design.

Value

A list with the valid-design input years, input and original cohort counts, design-field exclusions (a discharge can fail multiple fields), cohort criterion, and current domain count. Weighting fields describe the base weight column, annualization divisor, and whether supplied reweights were applied. The PSU and stratum fields name their year-scoped keys. For a fit, domain_n counts the records after any model subset and before the fit's missing-data action. The model entry gives the fitted unweighted count (n, from stats::nobs()) and the number of records the fit omitted for missing model data (excluded_n).

Details

Counts describe the input supplied to nis_design(). Filtering that input before making the design can change the sampling roster. Use a cohort expression or filter the design to restrict a survey domain. Review the counts for disclosure before sharing them.

See also

Other survey-design: nis_design(), nis_reweight(), nis_survey()

Examples

data <- nis_open(nis_example(2019:2020))
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpWkWQQQ/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpWkWQQQ/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
design <- nis_design(data, AGE >= 18, keep = c(AGE, LOS), annualize = TRUE)
#> Cohort: 192 discharges; weighted N 114.4; 24 hospitals across 2 years.
nis_design_report(design)
#> $years
#> [1] 2019 2020
#> 
#> $cohort
#> [1] "AGE >= 18"
#> 
#> $input_n
#> [1] 192
#> 
#> $excluded
#> $excluded$total
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $excluded$by_field

#>           0           0           0           0 
#> 
#> $excluded$by_year
#> # A tibble: 0 × 2
#> # ℹ 2 variables: YEAR <int>, n <dbl>
#> 
#> 
#> $cohort_n
#> [1] 192
#> 
#> $domain_n
#> [1] 192
#> 
#> $weight
#> [1] "DISCWT"
#> 
#> $psu
#> [1] "YEAR"     "HOSP_NIS"
#> 
#> $strata
#> [1] "YEAR"        "NIS_STRATUM"
#> 
#> $nest
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $annualize
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $divisor
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $reweighted
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $model
#> NULL
#> 
nis_design_report(survey::svyglm(LOS ~ AGE, design = design))
